title: The Present Simple
subtitle: Talk about your habits, routines and facts

beats.caption: Every morning, I <v>walk</v> to the hills with my cat.

say: I walk. My cat doesn't like. Mia is talking about her habits and about facts. This is the present simple, the most common tense in English.
Let's learn how to use it, and how to avoid the mistakes almost everyone makes.

data.heading: When do we use the present simple?
data.note: It's about what is generally true, not only now.

say: We use the present simple for things that are generally true.
Habits: I walk to school every day.
Routines: Grandma makes soup on Sundays.
Facts: water boils at a hundred degrees.
And timetables: the bus leaves at seven thirty.
So it's not about this moment. It's about what usually happens, or what is always true.
Mia lives in a small village. She has a black cat called Whiskers, and they go everywhere together.
beats.caption: Mia <v>lives</v> in a small village. She <v>has</v> a black cat.

data.heading: Form: add -s for he, she, it

say: The form is easy, with one important rule.
With I, you, we and they, use the base verb: I walk home.
With he, she and it, add s: she walks home. This little s is very important.
Have is special.
With he, she and it, it becomes has: Mia has a cat.
Spelling. Most verbs add s: read, reads.
Verbs ending in s, s h, c h, x or o add e s: watch, watches. Go, goes.
Consonant plus y changes to i e s: study, studies.
Vowel plus y just adds s: play, plays.
And remember: go, goes, and do, does.

data.heading: Saying -s: three sounds
data.tip: /ɪz/ after s, z, sh, ch, x

say: The s ending has three sounds, too.
After p, t, k and f, it sounds like s: walks, eats, likes, stops.
After voiced sounds, it sounds like z: plays, reads, lives, goes.
And after s, z, s h, c h and x, we add a syllable: watches, washes, kisses, fixes.
So: she watches, two syllables. But she walks, one syllable.
Every evening, Mia reads old maps in the attic. She loves stories about hidden places.
beats.caption: Every evening, Mia <v>reads</v> old maps. She <v>loves</v> stories.

say: Some words tell us how frequently something happens. They come before the main verb.
Always. Usually. Often.
Sometimes. Rarely. Never.
Whiskers always sits on the map. Mia never forgets her bag. But with be, they come after: she is always happy.

data.heading: Negative sentences
data.note: doesn't already has the -s: doesn't like (NOT doesn't likes)

say: For negatives, use don't with I, you, we and they, and doesn't with he, she and it. Then the base verb.
I don't like rain.
We don't watch TV.
She doesn't eat meat.
My cat doesn't like the rain.
Careful: doesn't already carries the s. So we say doesn't like, never doesn't likes.

data.heading: Questions and short answers
pairs: Yes, I do. / No, I don't.

say: For questions, use do or does before the subject, and the base verb.
Do you walk to school? Yes, I do. No, I don't.
Does Mia have a cat? Yes, she does.
Where do they live? They live in a village.
What does she read? She reads maps.

data.heading: Common mistakes (Arabic speakers)
rows: I am go to work every day.
I go to work every day.

say: Let's fix the most common mistakes.
She go to school. We need the s: she goes to school.
He don't like tea. With he, use doesn't: he doesn't like tea.
Does she likes cats? After does, the base verb: does she like cats?
I am go to work every day. We don't need am: I go to work every day.
She always is late. With be, always comes after: she is always late.

data.heading: Repeat after me
lines: I walk to school every day.

repeat.text: I walk to school every day.

say: Now say it with me. Listen, then repeat out loud.
Let's hear about Mia's week. Listen for the s, and for don't and doesn't.
Mia lives with her grandma. Every Sunday, Grandma makes soup and tells old stories.
beats.caption: Grandma <v>makes</v> soup and <v>tells</v> old stories.

say: After school, Mia often walks to the hills. She counts the sheep, and she doesn't go home before sunset.
beats.caption: Mia often <v>walks</v> to the hills. She <v>doesn't go</v> home before sunset.

data.heading: Your turn!
data.sub: Pause the video if you need more time

say: Quiz time. Five questions, five seconds each.

beats.say_answer: Lives. Mia is she, so we add s.
Does. Your cat is it, so we use does.
Watches. After c h we add e s.
I am always happy. With be, always comes after.

data.heading: Remember
items: he / she / it + s (has, goes, does)
always, never: before the verb (after be)

say: Let's remember. The present simple is for habits, routines, facts and timetables. Don't forget the s with he, she and it.
Use don't and doesn't for negatives, do and does for questions, always with the base verb.
And put frequency words before the main verb, but after be.
